title: Customer-facing chronology and self-serve reconciliation kit
body:
Purpose:
This draft is a customer-facing package to publish on the status page and send to affected tenants after the June 14th streaming fragmentation event (region: us-west-2). It includes: 1) short status-page text and an expanded customer email/update 2) a plain-language chronology of events 3) a concise technical summary and root cause explanation 4) self-serve reconciliation / replay steps customers can attempt immediately 5) verification checklist and recommended customer-side mitigations 6) contact/escalation information and next steps.

High-level status (ready-for-publish snippets):
- Short status (status.redwood.com update):
  - Title: Partial streaming fragmentation in us-west-2 — service degraded
  - Body: We experienced partial fragmentation affecting streaming responses in us-west-2 between 2028-06-14 03:42 UTC and 2028-06-14 04:25 UTC. Most requests succeeded; a subset of streaming sessions saw truncated fragments or missing final tokens. We have applied mitigations and restored normal service. If you observe missing output, use the replay steps below or contact support for manual reconciliation.

- Expanded customer update (email / console banner):
  - Opening: We’re sorry — on 2028-06-14 we had a partial degradation impacting streaming sessions in our us-west-2 region. While the platform remained partially available, some real-time streams were truncated or delivered incomplete final payloads. We’ve resolved the issue and validated service health, and this note explains why it happened and how you can self-serve recovery for affected requests.
  - Call-to-action: If you saw missing tokens or truncated streaming responses, please follow the Self-Serve Reconciliation Kit below. If you prefer, open a support case with evidence (request IDs, timestamps) and we will assist.

Plain-language chronology (customer-facing):
- 2028-06-14 03:42 UTC — Automated alert: increased rate of partial-stream timeouts observed for a small subset (approx 0.7%) of streaming sessions in us-west-2.
- 03:47 UTC — On-call begins investigation: traces show stream producers cut before final flush to client; backend indicated early KV-cache eviction on a small edge pool.
- 03:58 UTC — Temporary mitigation: routing rule updated to redirect new streaming sessions away from the affected pool. This reduced incidence but did not fix already-open sessions.
- 04:12 UTC — Patch deployed to server process to increase final-token flush timeout from 100ms to 300ms for the affected binary.
- 04:25 UTC — Monitoring confirms normal streaming completion rates; mitigation considered successful.
- 06:00 UTC — Full post-deployment verification completed; no data loss observed in persisted artifacts. Postmortem initiated.

Customer impact summary (what customers need to know):
- Scope: Affected tenants are those with streaming sessions routed to the impacted edge pool in us-west-2 between 03:42–04:25 UTC. Roughly 0.7% of streams in the region had truncated final output. Non-streaming (non-RT) generation and embeddings were unaffected.
- Data integrity: We verified that model state and persistent logs were not corrupted. There is no evidence of token loss in persisted outputs; the issue is truncated delivery to some clients.
- Recommended immediate action: Use the Self-Serve Reconciliation Kit below to re-request affected responses or request manual reconciliation from support.

Technical summary (brief, customer-facing):
- Root cause (simplified): An aggressive cache eviction heuristic on a small edge pool triggered during high short-lived session churn. Some in-flight streaming sessions experienced early KV cache evictions that prevented the final token batch from being flushed to clients.
- Why it affected streaming only: Streaming sessions maintain an in-memory KV/partial-output path optimized for low-latency flushes. The eviction policy prematurely reclaimed resources for a small subset of sessions, which did not occur for the standard non-streaming generation path.
- Mitigation implemented: 1) emergency routing to healthy pools, 2) increased final-token flush timeout and hardened eviction thresholds, 3) telemetry added to track flush success per-session.

Self-Serve Reconciliation Kit (step-by-step) — recommended for engineering teams:
1) Identify affected requests:
   - Look up request IDs and timestamps in your application logs for the time window 2028-06-14 03:42–04:25 UTC (us-west-2). If you have request IDs from the SDK/response events, collect those.
2) Try idempotent replay (preferred):
   - If your application maintains prompts/inputs, re-send the original request to the Redwood API with parameter replay=true (or include the original request_id if you saved it). Example: POST /v1/generate with body {"input": "<original-prompt>", "replay": true}. Replays will be routed to fresh pools and respect the latest model version pinned.
   - For chat-style sessions, include the final user message and the prior system messages; set streaming=false to receive the full final payload in a single response.
3) For streaming-first apps where you must preserve streaming semantics:
   - Re-open the session using the Console replay button (Console -> Tenants -> Request Logs -> Re-run) or via API with {"streaming": true, "replay": true}. The service will attempt to reproduce the output.
4) Manual reconciliation (if replay not possible):
   - Open a support case and attach: tenant_id, approximate timestamps, example request_id(s), and the original prompt text (or hashed prompt if data sensitivity is a concern). Support will escalate to engineering and can run targeted replays on your behalf.

Verification checklist (post-replay):
- Confirm that the replayed response contains the expected final tokens.
- If streaming=false was used, ensure the single response is not truncated.
- Compare length/hash of original expected output vs replayed output; flag differences >2% for review.
- Save request_id(s) from successful replay for audit trail.

Sample status page text (concise + expanded):
- Concise: "Resolved — Partial streaming fragmentation in us-west-2. Some streaming sessions saw truncated output; mitigations applied. See post-incident guidance for self-serve replay steps."
- Expanded (for email/console): [see "Expanded customer update" above].

Customer FAQ (anticipated):
Q: Will I be billed again if I replay those requests?
A: Replays are billed according to normal usage. If a tenant demonstrates a material number of failed deliveries due to the incident, we will evaluate targeted credits on a case-by-case basis; please include evidence in your support ticket.

Q: Could the replay produce a different model output?
A: Model outputs are not strictly deterministic; small differences are possible due to nondeterminism, model version, or sampling parameters. If you need strict determinism for reconciliation, include deterministic settings (temperature=0, seed if supported) in replay requests and note them in the support case.

Q: Is data lost?
A: No persistent data loss was detected. The issue is delivery truncation to some clients. All persisted logs and model state validate correctly.

Escalation & contacts:
- Primary: Aisha Carter (Customer Success Lead) — aisha@redwood.com — include ticket JIRA-INC-1245 in subject
- On-call engineering: Luca Moreno (serving-runtime lead) — luca@redwood.com
- Support intake link: https://support.redwood.com/cases/new (attach request ids and timestamps)

Action items (internal, tracked):
- [ENG] Add per-session flush telemetry and create an alert for >0.2% flush failures across any pool — owner: Luca Moreno — due 2028-06-18
- [PLAT] Update eviction heuristic and roll to all edge pools, include canary plan — owner: Priya Shah — due 2028-06-21
- [CS] Send targeted tenant emails for customers with >5 affected streams — owner: Aisha Carter — due 2028-06-16
- [DOCS] Add replay examples to public docs and SDK quickstarts (both streaming and non-streaming) — owner: Benji Li — due 2028-06-23

Notes / internal annotations (drafty):
- PM wants an estimate of number of unique tenants affected (Luca to provide), also list of enterprise customers with SSO bypasses.
- Consider a short tenants-only webinar to walk through replay and deterministic reconciliation if there are many enterprise requests.
- TODO: cross-check billing ledger for replays during window and mark suspicious charges for review.

Last checked: 2028-06-20 19:00 UTC — monitoring shows no elevated flush failures across any region.

Document history: 2028-06-15 initial draft by Aisha; 2028-06-16 added internal action owners; 2028-06-20 final review and telemetry confirmation notes added by Luca.

End of customer package.
